item.title: When Is Each Part Happy?
item.description:
When Is Each Part Happy?

Denna

  • (Constructive change) I feel happy when some destructive pattern is changed into a constructive one; because it hurts to know that people are suffering because of what other human beings are doing.
  • When things are quiet

Ava

  • I feel happy when I'm moving around, but I don't have to be moving around
  • Playing fast physical games, like mountain biking and dirt biking and, I don't know, stuff like that.
  • Feeling a connection with other people.
    • Sometimes I feel sad because I find it very difficult to connect with anyone.
    • Sometimes I feel like there really isn't even one person who really deeply understands me.

Jadie

  • I feel happy when there are things that are soft, not sharp.
  • Happy bright colors

Cara

  • I feel at least ok when I have time to think
  • When Denna talked about, what I call positive change, that resonated with me.

Sara

  • I never thought about what makes me happy before
  • I feel happy when things are quiet
  • I feel happy doing little precise things with my hands and eyes or visualizing

Cole

  • Luna
    • The way he is, that is a good way
  • I don't usually think about what makes me happy, I just think about what I have to do. Maybe I need to change that so my body feels better; negative emotions eat away at the immune system, some scientists say.
  • Sometimes, the sadness overwhelms me to the point where I don't even think about anything happy.
  • I should remember to focus on the solution, not the problem.

Janet

  • I just focus on what needs fixing, but like Cole, I ought to think about the things that make me happy more often.
  • Coffee!
  • When all our parts love each other and we are all there with each other
    • I trust us

Nicole

  • "I don't know Brooke, I don't think I ever think about that either; survival mode."
  • I am happy, for starters, if I can exist in peace, and if I can know that others also are existing in peace.

Rose

  • All the usual stuff makes me happy.
  • I just like being here too, like Janet was talking about, you know, because of our parts.
  • Do some Drupal work and get some money to do some bigger stuff, more stuff, maybe some fun stuff.
  • Using our imagination makes us happy. We can visualize just about anything; we should do that more often.

item.title: Matt Pocock's Wayfinder Skill Notes
item.description:
Matt Pocock's Wayfinder Skill Notes

Wayfinder Workflow

  • Use /wayfinder <prompt> to create a map with decision issues.
  • Wayfinder will ask you choose a destination: a buildable spec or an actual product.
  • After wayfinder has made the initial map, work through issues one at a time using /wayfinder <ticket number> until all decisions are made. Sometimes new issues will be created while working on other issues.
  • Wayfinder will utilize other skills, such as /grill-with-docs, /prototype, and /research.
    • The map specifies when each of those other skills are to be used
  • The map also includes a list of 4 types of decision tickets:
    • research
    • prototype
    • grilling
    • task (things the agent can't quite do itself)
  • Once the map is made, then you can use /to-spec to turn the map into a spec.
  • Then use /to-tickets to create implementation tickets from the spec.
  • Use /implement to implement one ticket at at time
  • Use /implement-spec to have agents implement the whole spec AFK
  • Use /code-review afterward
  • Use /retro afterward to have the agent document what could have went better in the session.

Other mattpocock/skills that are helpful

  • /handoff: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document so another agent can continue the work.
  • /teach: Teach the user a new skill or concept over multiple sessions, using the current directory as a stateful teaching workspace.
  • /wait-what: Fire this the moment a message doesn't land.
  • /to-questionnaire: Turn a decision you can't answer alone into a Markdown questionnaire for the one person who can, filled in async, or together over a meeting. It grills you about the send (who it's for, what you need back), not the subject.

Addons for base Drupal configurations

Descriptions of 4 common ways to setup DDEV

Add-onBest forTypical project layout
UltraBob/ddev-drupal-code-qualityFull Drupal website projects where your site repo already contains Drupal code and custom code.Existing site/project repo; installs code-quality configs and IDE shims in-place.
ddev/ddev-drupal-contribDrupal contrib module/theme development where the contrib project is the center of the repo.Contrib project repo with Drupal scaffolded around it (symlink workflow).
justafish/ddev-drupal-core-dev / joachim-n/ddev-drupal-core-devDrupal core development.Drupal core checkout or core-dev project template.
https://addons.ddev.com/addons/amateescu/ddev-drupal-devDrupal core and contrib combined, see belowcore git checkout as the project root.

DDEV Drupal Dev from Andrei Mateescu of Tag1

A DDEV add-on for working on Drupal core and contrib modules together, using a core git checkout as the project root.

Other add-ons target either core or contrib in isolation. This one is for when you need both: developing a contrib module against the latest core, fixing a core bug that affects contrib, or running contrib tests on a core patch.

Extra dependencies (contrib modules, Drush, dev tools) are managed through a composer.local.json overlay, keeping core's composer.json and composer.lock untouched.

"You can work on multiple modules this way; each gets its own git checkout that you can commit and push to independently."

item.title: Contrib Drupal Module Development
item.description:
Contrib Drupal Module Development

One way to set up local Development for a contrib module using e0ipso's AI suite. See Agentic Coding Harness for Drupal 

  • opt out of T3 telemetry by adding the following to ~/.ddev/.env
    • T3CODE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false
  • Install https://github.com/e0ipso/self-review
  • Then:
BDEV_CURRENT_SITE="config_suite"
cd ~/Sites
git clone git@git.drupal.org:project/$BDEV_CURRENT_SITE.git
cd $BDEV_CURRENT_SITE
cp ~/projects/.gitignore-ddev .gitignore
ddev config --project-type=drupal11 --docroot=web
orb
ddev add-on get ddev/ddev-drupal-contrib
ddev add-on get hanoii/ddev-drupal-contrib-extras
ddev start
ddev poser

ddev symlink-project
ddev config --update
ddev restart
ddev drush si -y
ddev drush en $BDEV_CURRENT_SITE -y
open $(ddev drush uli)
ddev exec "cd web/core && yarn install"

# Temporary workaround on Mac because e0ipso's plugin only works for Linux for importing local OpenCode config
mkdir -p $HOME/Sites/$BDEV_CURRENT_SITE/.ddev/homeadditions/.local/share
ln -s $HOME/.local/share/opencode $HOME/Sites/$BDEV_CURRENT_SITE/.ddev/homeadditions/.local/share/opencode

ddev add-on get e0ipso/ddev-playwright-cli
ddev add-on get e0ipso/ddev-assistant-opencode
ddev add-on get e0ipso/ddev-assistant-t3
ddev restart

# Allows running playwright-cli from inside the container
#   without having to use the --config option
# Symlinks .claude playwright skills to .agents folder for other harnesses. 
ddev ssh

rm .playwright/cli.config.json
ln -s "$(pwd)/.ddev/playwright-cli/cli.config.json" .playwright/cli.config.json
mkdir -p .agents/skills
ln -s "$(pwd)/.claude/skills/playwright-cli" .agents/skills/playwright-cli
exit

npx kenkeep init --harnesses opencode
npx kenkeep doctor
npx kenkeep pack import e0ipso/kenkeep-pack-drupal
npx strikethroo init --harnesses opencode
npx skills add e0ipso/strikethroo

Strikethroo workflow: https://strikethroo.canpicasoft.com/workflow.html Kenkeep docs: https://kenkeep.canpicasoft.com/

  • ddev t3 start
  • npx strikethroo serve
  • /st-create-plan display a welcome message to new users
  • /st-refine-plan 1, see review.xml
  • /st-execute-blueprint 1
  • /st-code-review 1, line 95 in example.module has a typo: "piece" should be "peace"

item.title: Notes for: Site Analysis and AI's Strengths and Limits, By David Hobbs
item.description:
Notes for: Site Analysis and AI's Strengths and Limits, By David Hobbs

Just copying over some notes from a great video, in case it ever goes away:

 

Site Analysis and AI's Strengths and Limits

By David Hobbs

Progression of content analysis

#TypeExampleAutomation at scale?Use Al?Quantitative or

Qualitative?
1Traditional AutomationCrawl with [[Screaming Frog]]YesNoQuantitative
2ManualLine-by-line qualitative auditNoNoQualitative
3One-off AlAsk ChatGPT a question about a siteNoYes, one timeQualitative
4LLM → DeterministicHave Claude write a script to run reading level analysis on every pagePartialYes, one timeQuantitative
5Scaled AlPass thousands of pages to low power LLM to categorizeYesYes, every pageQualitative
Note: Al allows us to do some qualitative analysis that is NOT manual.     

Advantages of particular types of content analysis

   
#TypeAdvantages
1Traditional AutomationEasy to get basic information on many pages.
2ManualThe approach everyone knows, and it feels like things are being done in a high quality manner (even before Al this was often the feeling).
3One-off AlEasy to get analysis that might be outside your expertise for a subset of pages.
4LLM → DeterministicOnly use Al once, and then have all the advantages of traditional automation.
5Scaled AlGet qualitative information over a large swath of content (possibly impossible otherwise).

Disadvantages of the manual approach

  • ﻿﻿Almost certainly leads to restricting the number of pages that are analyzed.
  • ﻿﻿Very difficult to iterate or change course (such as if you decide to change the definition of audience)
  • ﻿﻿Very difficult to merge analysis from multiple people.
  • ﻿﻿Very difficult to be consistent.
  • ﻿﻿Difficult to track over time.
  • ﻿﻿Likely to encourage team to take action on content while analyzing it.

Disadvantages of one-off Al

  • ﻿﻿Generally low transparency (How did it come up with the answer? Did it look at any pages? Did it consider your existing analysis?)
  • ﻿﻿Related to the above, it can definitely hallucinate or over-extrapolate.
  • ﻿﻿Generally requires powerful LLM
  • ﻿﻿Can short circuit critical thinking of the analyst
  • ﻿﻿NOT for pervasive analysis across a digital presence

Tip: If you do one-off chatbot analysis, explicitly ask how it came up with the answer and its sources. ie., "Explain to me in detail how you determined this. What sources did you use? What did you derive from each source? What confidence do you have in this answer?"

Disadvantages of LLM → Deterministic

  • ﻿﻿Depending on skillset, can be difficult to evaluate whether the script is doing what you want it to do
  • ﻿﻿Can be difficult to clearly specify the requirements
  • ﻿﻿One-off efforts to write scripts can be difficult to reconcile together into a coherent whole

Keep in mind non-LLM automated analysis options

  • ﻿﻿Near-text duplicate analysis
  • ﻿﻿Graph database analysis (analysis of linkages between content / sections)
  • ﻿﻿Scraping out information and component analysis
  • ﻿﻿PDF analysis
  • ﻿﻿Merge information (for instance from Google Analytics)
  • ﻿﻿Reading level analysis
  • ﻿﻿Charting
  • ﻿﻿HTML structure analysis
  • ﻿﻿Over-time analysis
  • ﻿﻿Logo analysis
  • ﻿﻿Formulas, maps, and rules
  • ﻿﻿Technology analysis (such as with wappalyzer)

Tip: Consider converting problems to deterministic ones with AI

Disadvantage of Scaled Al

  • ﻿﻿Difficult to develop on your own
  • ﻿﻿Heavy processing is in the backend (not in chatbot)

TIp: Clearly differentiate between what's EASY to analyze and what's IMPORTANT to analyze.

Note: Far too often teams just revert to what's simple to analyze when that will not help them achieve their real business goals. For example, you can't analyze for consolidation if you only look at a small subset of pages because then you would be able to use a spreadsheet.

Summary

  • ﻿﻿There is lots of automation that can be applied outside of LLMs.
  • ﻿﻿For some questions, you really do need to look at the entire digital presence.
  • ﻿﻿Al can help you accomplish qualitative assessments that required manual intervention before.
    There are a variety of ways of using Al for site analysis.

Tips

  1. ﻿﻿﻿Focus on refining the QUESTIONS you need answered.
  2. ﻿﻿﻿If you do one-off chatbot analysis, explicitly ask how it came up with the answer in its sources.
  3. ﻿﻿﻿Consider converting problems to deterministic ones with Al.
  4. ﻿﻿﻿Clearly differentiate between what's EASY to analyze and what's IMPORTANT to analyze.

item.title: AI Ethics
item.description:
AI Ethics

The Environment

From When the Clock Ticks Closer: AI, Ethics, and Drupal's Responsibility to the Public Good April 1, 2026

  • Data centers are multiplying across the globe drawing enormous quantities of power and water
  • from communities already under resource strain.
  • The raw materials required for AI hardware involve
    • environmentally damaging extraction processes
    • energy-intensive manufacturing
    • growing mountains of electronic waste

"This is not an abstraction for the Drupal community. As an ecosystem that powers a substantial share of the world's web infrastructure - from small nonprofits to national governments - the collective energy footprint of Drupal-based sites and the hosting decisions behind them carries real weight. Organizations within the community have begun pushing for greener hosting choices, leaner architectures, and more deliberate thinking about when AI features add genuine value versus when they simply add compute."

item.title: Context Control Center (ai_context)
item.description:
Context Control Center (ai_context)
  • 2026-10-08 Context Control Center: Bringing AI Context Natively to Drupal CMS
  • 2026-09-11 Context Control Center: Teaching Drupal AI Your House Rules with Kristen Pol
  • 2026-08-24 Drupal AI: Context Control Center update and demo, August 2026

It's important to know that context items are Drupal content entities. So, they get moderation, revisions, scheduling, multilingual support, and more.

Context examples

  • Brand Guidelines
  • Taglines & Slogans
  • Pricing & Packages
  • A11y Standards
  • Case Studies
  • Tone of Voice
  • Audience Personas
  • FAQS
  • SEO Data
  • Client Quotes
  • Writing Rules
  • Journey Maps
  • Glossary
  • Content Templates
  • Partner List
  • Editorial Guide
  • Product List
  • Compliance Rules
  • Landing Page Rules
  • Privacy Policies
  • Service Catalog
  • Legal Disclaimers
  • Campaign Briefs
  • Language Rules

Overview of Context Management

The module provides a way to create "Context Items" with moderation, revisions, scheduling, multilingual support, and markdown editing in a Drupal CMS-native Ul.

Context Scope Plugins

Categorize context with agents subscribing to the most relevant scopes, all of which are plugins.

Scope: Applies Everywhere

  • Global

Scope: Chosen By People

  • Context Tags
  • Use Cases

Scope: Detected from Page, User, etc.

  • Site Sections
  • Languages
  • Role
  • Specific Entities
  • Entity Types
  • Taxonomy Terms

Consumers

  • Agent
  • Automater
  • AI CKEditor

Subcontext

Subcontexts group items into a one-level hierarchy, with children always included or LLM-selected based on relevance.

Context Selection

Controls what each agent receives via scopes, entity targeting, and inclusion rules, with configurable item and token limits.

Admin Experience

Includes a lightweight dashboard, usage tracking, access control, and configurable settings for scopes and moderation.

Developer Experience

Includes debug logging, agent debugging tools, comprehensive test coverage, and detailed documentation.

Three steps to your first context item

Install

composer require drupal/ai_context drush en
Requires the Al and AI Agents modules and a configured provider.

Add sample context

drush recipe modules/contrib/ai_context/recipes/ai_context_demo_university
Unpublished university examples you can edit, copy, or learn from.

Open the overview

/admin/config/ai/context
Onboarding page with links to items, consumers, scopes, and usage.

Notes

One of the ways the context can be scoped is you can create "Custom Sections", then when you create context items, you can sort of tag them with that scope.
